properties.name: MEASURED on real RocksDB with a RELEASE binary: the two calls documented as cheap orientation reads cost ~11.5s each, and ~10s of that is detect_defects riding along on a reply nobody asked it of
properties.statement:
🛑 **CLOSED 2026-08-23 — THE MEASUREMENT BELOW IS HISTORY. Read it as taken on 2026-08-21 and since superseded. It is kept in full because the METHOD is worth more than the numbers.**

WHAT RETIRED IT: PR #290, `chg:the-spof-sweep-stops-rebuilding-its-graph`. The single-point-of-failure sweep was rebuilding TWO full operational networks per candidate. After: **56 candidates at 878ms each became 5.08ms for all 56; `detect_structural_defects` 44.5s → 4.43s; `open_questions` — the first call of every session — 11.7s → 2.95s**, with the answer unchanged at 54 defects and 13 structural issues.

⇒ THREE CLAIMS BELOW WERE FALSE from the day #290 merged: *"NOTHING WAS OPTIMISED"*, *"that ratio is the next measurement and it has not been taken"*, and the 11.7s figure for `open_questions`. The 20x `detect_defects`/`detect_gaps` ratio WAS investigated and WAS fixed.

⭐⭐ **THIS NODE IS WHY `req:the-graph-can-say-what-has-already-been-done` EXISTS.** On 2026-08-23 an agent asked where else to optimise, read this fact, and quoted all three false claims back as current. Anthony corrected it — *"I think we already determined candidate 3"* — and he was right while the graph was wrong. He then generalised the cost: on a shared design, one person finishing a task and another repeating it produces **two solutions from two users**, which is not a graph merge.

📌 THE FIRST FINDING CLOSED UNDER `capture-session`'s test 7, added the same day and exercised here for the first time. Two things went wrong in the closing and both are worth keeping: the closure was FIRST written by REPLACING this statement, destroying the measurement it was closing — caught by the tool's own "no snapshot holds the prior value" warning, restored, snapshotted via `record_change`, and re-applied. **Closing a finding must PRESERVE it: a closed measurement is evidence, an erased one is a hole.** That is the failure mode test 7 will keep producing until the skill says so.

═══════════════ THE MEASUREMENT AS TAKEN, 2026-08-21 ═══════════════

MEASURED through the REAL MCP tool surface, driven over stdio against a REAL RocksDB store built from reflow2's own committed export (2862 nodes, 12139 edges, 8 MB on disk). Both build profiles, because users run release binaries and developers run debug.

                      debug      RELEASE
  get_node            0.01s       0.00s
  scan_nodes          0.11s       0.01s
  export_graph        3.10s       0.36s
  detect_gaps         3.11s       0.51s
  detect_defects     40.8s       10.3s     <== the hot spot
  loop_status        47.5s       11.4s
  open_questions     50.6s       11.7s     <== the FIRST call of every session
  graph_report    45–92s       10.9–22.4s

⭐ THE FINDING: `detect_defects` COSTS ~10s AND RIDES ALONG ON CALLS THAT NEVER ASKED FOR IT. `loop_status` reports a structural-defect count so it pays; `open_questions` pays it through the `loop_hint` attached to its reply. `open_questions` does its own work in about half a second and cost 11.7. So the two calls this project's own instructions call the cheap orientation reads were the two most expensive on the surface, and neither was expensive because of what it was asked to do.

🛑 AND IT CORRECTED A STANDING BELIEF. "The first store read of a session costs 26–48s" had been carried as a known cost and read as the STORE being slow. It was not the store: `get_node` is sub-millisecond and `scan_nodes` 10ms on the real backend. The cost was a whole-design sweep bolted onto an orientation reply.

TWO HYPOTHESES FALSIFIED FIRST, both cheap, both recorded so nobody re-runs them:
(1) THAT THE SYNC CHECK WAS READING AND HASHING EVERY KNOWN EXPORT FILE. `sync_debt` does exactly that per path in `last_synced`, and this design has ~15 such paths, several at 7.5 MB. FALSIFIED: a probe store with `last_synced` EMPTY still took 46.5s.
(2) THAT `export_graph` INSIDE THE DEBT COMPUTATION WAS THE COST. FALSIFIED: 3.1s debug, 0.36s release.

The cause was found by timing each tool in an ISOLATED fresh process, which also ruled out ordering and cache effects — `detect_gaps` measured 3.11 / 3.06 / 3.11 while `open_questions` measured 50.59 / 50.44 / 50.86.

⚠️ BOUND AS STATED THEN: one machine, one design, one shape of design. The RATIOS were the transferable part; the absolute seconds were not — and the ratios are what moved.
